questions.q: Which of the following predicts the failure stress reasonably well for brittle materials under static biaxial loading?
questions.e: Maximum normal stress (Rankine) theory: a brittle part fails when the largest principal stress reaches the ultimate strength. Von Mises and maximum shear are ductile-yield criteria. (Coulomb-Mohr is a refinement for brittle materials with different tensile and compressive strengths.)

x.A: A brittle part fails when its largest principal stress reaches the ultimate strength, which is why this theory fits brittle materials.
x.B: Coulomb-Mohr refines the prediction for brittle materials with different tensile and compressive strengths, but it is not the basic theory asked for.
x.C: Von Mises is a ductile yield criterion based on distortion energy.
x.D: Maximum shear stress is a ductile yield criterion.

questions.q: In the absence of friction, a simple machine is an ideal machine if the efficiency is
questions.e: Efficiency = output work / input work. With no friction there are no losses, so efficiency = 1 (100%).

x.A: Real machines with friction have efficiency below 1.
x.B: With no friction there are no losses, so output work equals input work and efficiency is 1.
x.C: An efficiency of zero would mean the machine delivers no output at all.
x.D: Efficiency above 1 would create energy, which is impossible.

questions.q: Which of the following is a form of an inclined plane?
questions.e: A screw is an inclined plane wrapped around a cylinder (a helical ramp).

x.A: A pulley is a wheel with a rope and works like a lever, not an inclined plane.
x.B: A screw is an inclined plane wrapped around a cylinder, a helical ramp.
x.C: A lever is a rigid bar turning about a fulcrum.
x.D: A wheel and axle is a rotating lever-type machine.

questions.q: What is the ideal mechanical advantage of a machine that changes only the direction of the input force?
questions.e: Output force equals input force (e.g., a fixed pulley), so IMA = 1.

x.A: A value below 1 means the output force is smaller than the input force.
x.B: If a machine only changes direction, the output force equals the input force, so IMA is 1 (like a fixed pulley).
x.C: An IMA of zero would mean no force is delivered.
x.D: A value above 1 means the force is multiplied, not just redirected.

questions.q: Ackermann steering gear is made up of
questions.e: The Ackermann gear is a four-bar linkage with turning (revolute) pairs only. The Davis gear is the one with sliding pairs.

x.A: Sliding and rotary pairs are found in the Davis steering gear.
x.B: Rolling pairs are not what the Ackermann linkage uses.
x.C: The Ackermann gear is a four-bar linkage with turning (revolute) pairs only.
x.D: Rolling and sliding pairs are not part of the Ackermann linkage.

questions.q: What is the meaning of the “U” stamp on a pressure vessel?
c: It meets ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code requirements
It is approved for nuclear-grade service
It has passed ultrasonic testing only
It is intended for low-temperature operation
questions.e: The ASME “U” stamp certifies the vessel was designed, fabricated and inspected per the ASME BPV Code (Section VIII).

x.A: The U stamp certifies the vessel was designed, fabricated and inspected to the ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code (Section VIII).
x.B: Nuclear components use different ASME stamps, not the U stamp.
x.C: Ultrasonic testing is an inspection method, not what the stamp stands for.
x.D: The U stamp does not indicate a service temperature.

questions.q: Which failure mode is most critical for long, slender columns under compressive load?
questions.e: Slender columns fail by sudden lateral instability (buckling) well before the material yields.

x.A: Slender columns fail by sudden sideways instability (buckling) well before the material yields.
x.B: Yielding governs short, stocky columns, not long slender ones.
x.C: Fatigue needs repeated loading, not a steady compressive load.
x.D: Shear failure is not the main mode for a slender column.

questions.q: What is the term for the ratio of a column's effective length to its radius of gyration?
questions.e: Slenderness ratio = Le / r, where r is the radius of gyration.

x.A: The slenderness ratio is the effective length divided by the radius of gyration.
x.B: Aspect ratio compares the width and height of a shape.
x.C: Shape factor compares plastic and elastic section moduli.
x.D: Stress ratio compares the minimum and maximum stress in a fatigue cycle.

questions.q: Which support condition provides both vertical reaction and moment resistance?
questions.e: A fixed support restrains translation and rotation, so it gives reactions in both directions and a moment. Pin: forces only. Roller: one force only.

x.A: A fixed support restrains translation and rotation, so it gives force reactions and a moment.
x.B: A roller gives one force reaction perpendicular to the surface and no moment.
x.C: A pin gives force reactions only, with no moment.
x.D: A link gives a single force along its length.

questions.q: What is the combination of applied normal and shear stresses that produces the maximum principal normal stress or minimum principal normal stress, with a third principal stress between or equivalent to the extremes?
questions.e: Principal normal stresses are the maximum and minimum normal stresses acting on planes with zero shear stress.

x.A: Principal shear stress is the maximum shear on a plane, not the extreme normal stress.
x.B: Principal normal stresses are the maximum and minimum normal stresses on planes with zero shear.
x.C: Maximum shear stress is a different stress quantity.
x.D: Bending and shear are types of loading, not stress extremes.

questions.q: What is the other term for the Maximum-Shear-Stress Theory, as a failure prediction theory?
questions.e: The Tresca criterion is the maximum shear stress theory: yielding starts when τmax reaches Sy/2. Von Mises is the distortion-energy theory.

x.A: Von Mises is the distortion-energy theory, a different criterion.
x.B: The Tresca criterion is the maximum shear stress theory: yielding starts when τmax reaches Sy/2.
x.C: Coulomb-Mohr is a theory for brittle materials.
x.D: Modified Mohr is also a brittle-material theory.

questions.q: In planar kinematics, what is the locus of points on a moving body that exhibits zero rate of change of curvature at a given instant?
questions.e: The cubic of stationary curvature is the locus of points whose path curvature is momentarily stationary. The inflection circle is the locus of points with zero curvature (instantaneous straight-line motion).

x.A: The cubic of stationary curvature is the locus of points whose path curvature is momentarily stationary.
x.B: The fixed centrode is the locus of instant centers in the fixed plane.
x.C: The inflection circle is the locus of points with zero curvature (instantaneous straight-line motion).
x.D: An evolute is the locus of centers of curvature of a path.

questions.q: Which of the following is the ratio of the fatigue strength without a stress concentration to the fatigue strength with a stress concentration?
questions.e: Kf = fatigue strength of unnotched specimen / fatigue strength of notched specimen.

x.A: Notch sensitivity q = (Kf − 1)/(Kt − 1) is a different quantity.
x.B: The factor of safety compares strength with applied stress.
x.C: A reliability factor adjusts endurance strength for statistical reliability.
x.D: The fatigue stress concentration factor Kf is the unnotched fatigue strength divided by the notched fatigue strength.

questions.q: This is a theory in cyclic and impact loading which states that damage at any stress level is proportional to the number of cycles. What is this theory commonly called?
questions.e: Miner's rule (linear cumulative damage): D = Σ ni/Ni, with failure when D = 1.

x.A: Miner's rule is linear cumulative damage: D = Σ n/N, failing at D = 1.
x.B: The Paris law describes crack growth rate.
x.C: The Goodman rule corrects for mean stress.
x.D: Manson-Coffin relates strain to life in low-cycle fatigue.

questions.q: A storage tank for saline water requires a material that is lightweight, corrosion-resistant, and has good mechanical strength. Which material is the most suitable choice?
questions.e: 6061 aluminum best matches all three needs (low weight, corrosion resistance, good strength). 316 stainless resists chlorides but is much heavier; carbon and galvanized steel corrode.

x.A: 6061 aluminum is light, corrosion-resistant and strong, matching all three needs.
x.B: Galvanized steel is heavy, and its zinc coat corrodes in saline water.
x.C: Medium carbon steel is heavy and corrodes in saline water.
x.D: 316 stainless resists chlorides but is much heavier, so it fails the lightweight need.

questions.q: It is one of the rigid members/bodies joined together to form a kinematic chain.
questions.e: A link is a rigid body (or resistant body) connected to others by joints to form a kinematic chain.

x.A: Coplanar describes motion in one plane; it is not a part of a chain.
x.B: A link is a rigid body joined to others to form a kinematic chain.
x.C: A frame is the fixed link of a mechanism.
x.D: A machine is the whole assembly, not one member.

questions.q: For a kinematic chain to be considered as a mechanism
c: None of the links should be fixed
questions.e: Fixing one link (the frame) turns a kinematic chain into a mechanism.

x.A: If no link is fixed, the chain is free to move as a whole.
x.B: Fixing one link (the frame) turns a kinematic chain into a mechanism.
x.C: Fixing two links would stop it from moving.
x.D: There is such a criterion: one link must be fixed.

questions.q: The mechanism used to enlarge or reduce movements for reproducing drawings to different scales is called
questions.e: A pantograph is a parallelogram-based linkage that copies a drawing at a different scale.

x.A: A clinograph measures inclination; it does not copy drawings.
x.B: A trisquare is a drafting square.
x.C: A graphometer is a surveying instrument for angles.
x.D: A pantograph is a parallelogram linkage that copies a drawing at a different scale.

questions.q: In gramophones for adjusting the speed of the turn-table, what type of governor is commonly used?
questions.e: The Pickering governor (leaf-spring type) is used in gramophones and phonographs.

x.A: The Hartung governor is a spring-loaded engine governor.
x.B: Inertia governors are a different type used on engines.
x.C: The Pickering governor uses leaf springs and is used in gramophones to hold turntable speed.
x.D: The Wilson-Hartnell governor is a spring-controlled engine governor.

questions.q: What beam is carried by three or more supports, allowing the bending effects to be distributed along its span?
questions.e: A continuous beam spans over three or more supports.

x.A: A continuous beam rests on three or more supports.
x.B: A cantilever is fixed at one end and free at the other.
x.C: A propped cantilever is fixed at one end with one added support.
x.D: A fixed beam is fixed at both ends.

questions.q: Which beam-section property is used as the ratio of moment of inertia to the distance from the neutral axis to the extreme fiber?
questions.e: Section modulus S = I/c.

x.A: Section modulus is S = I/c, the moment of inertia over the distance to the extreme fiber.
x.B: Polar moment of inertia relates to torsion.
x.C: Slenderness ratio is the effective length over the radius of gyration.
x.D: Modulus of elasticity is a material stiffness, not a section property.

questions.q: For a compression member, what property is increased when the diameter of the column is made larger?
questions.e: A larger diameter raises I and lowers the slenderness ratio, so the critical load (Pcr = π²EI/L²) increases.

x.A: A larger diameter raises the moment of inertia and lowers the slenderness ratio, so buckling resistance goes up.
x.B: Torsional shear stress is a shaft property and decreases as diameter grows.
x.C: Bearing pressure drops as the contact area grows, not increases.
x.D: Surface hardness is a material property.

questions.q: In a beam under bending, what is the axis where the normal bending stress becomes zero?
questions.e: Bending stress varies linearly from the neutral axis (zero stress), which passes through the centroid for elastic bending.

x.A: The neutral axis is where bending stress is zero.
x.B: The shear center is the point where a load causes no twisting.
x.C: Principal axes are the axes of maximum and minimum moment of inertia.
x.D: The elastic curve is the deflected shape of the beam.

questions.q: If an eccentric compressive load acts within the kern of a column section, what stress condition exists over the whole cross-section?
c: Entire section is subjected to shear
Section becomes stress-free at the edge
questions.e: Within the kern (core) the bending stress never exceeds the direct compressive stress, so no tension develops anywhere.

x.A: If the load is inside the kern, the whole section stays in compression.
x.B: One side goes into tension only if the load is outside the kern.
x.C: Shear is not the stress condition across the section.
x.D: The edge becomes stress-free only exactly at the kern boundary.

questions.q: It is also known as the diamond pyramid hardness test, uses a pyramid-shaped diamond indenter and a load that ranges from 1 kg to 120 kg.
questions.e: The Vickers test uses a square-based diamond pyramid. Knoop uses an elongated pyramid; Brinell uses a steel ball.

x.A: The Vickers test uses a square-based diamond pyramid and is also called diamond pyramid hardness.
x.B: Mohs is a scratch scale for minerals.
x.C: The Knoop test uses an elongated diamond pyramid.
x.D: The Brinell test uses a steel ball.

questions.q: “For a planar four-bar linkage, the sum of the shortest and longest lengths cannot be greater than the sum of the remaining two link lengths if there is to be a continuous relative rotation between two members.” How do you call the preceding statement?
questions.e: Grashof's law: s + l ≤ p + q.

x.A: Grubler's equation gives degrees of freedom, not this law.
x.B: Coriolis is about the acceleration component in rotating frames, not link lengths.
x.C: Grashof's law: the shortest plus longest link must not exceed the sum of the other two for continuous rotation.
x.D: Freudenstein's equation is used to synthesize four-bar linkages.

questions.q: It is a Grashof four-bar mechanism in which the shortest link is the frame or fixed link and the other two cranks completely rotate with their axes. How do you call this Grashof four-bar mechanism?
questions.e: Shortest link fixed gives a double-crank (drag-link) mechanism. Shortest link as the crank gives a crank-rocker; shortest link as the coupler gives a double-rocker.

x.A: In a drag-link mechanism the shortest link is fixed and both cranks rotate fully.
x.B: In a double-rocker the shortest link is the coupler.
x.C: In a crank-rocker the shortest link is the crank.
x.D: A triple-rocker is a non-Grashof linkage, where no link rotates fully.

questions.q: The motion of a shaft in a circular hole is an example of ______ motion.
questions.e: The shaft can both rotate and slide along the hole, so the motion depends on the applied force direction: incompletely constrained motion.

x.A: Successful constraint means external forces keep the motion definite, as with a piston.
x.B: Completely constrained motion allows only one possible motion.
x.C: Free motion has no constraint.
x.D: A shaft in a round hole can rotate and slide, so its motion depends on the applied force: incompletely constrained.

questions.q: Which property best distinguishes a ductile material from a brittle one when analyzing a stress-strain diagram?
c: Greater energy absorption prior to fracture
questions.e: Ductile materials show a large plastic region, so a large area under the curve (toughness) before fracture. Brittle materials fracture with little deformation.

x.A: Ductile materials absorb more energy before fracture because of their large plastic region.
x.B: Stiffness (modulus) does not separate ductile from brittle.
x.C: Yield strength can be high or low in either kind.
x.D: Sudden fracture without deformation describes a brittle material.

questions.q: In vibration analysis, which parameter governs the natural frequency of a simple spring–mass system?
questions.e: ωn = √(k/m).

x.A: The natural frequency is the square root of stiffness over mass: ωn = √(k/m).
x.B: The ratio of mass to stiffness is inverted and lacks the square root.
x.C: Stiffness times displacement is a force, not a frequency.
x.D: Frequency depends on stiffness as well, not on mass alone.

questions.q: Which superalloy is commonly utilized as a stainless-type material due to its high yield strength?
questions.e: Marked answer: Allegheny Ludlum alloy. Nimonic and Inconel are nickel-base alloys for high-temperature service; Nitralloy is a nitriding steel.

x.A: Marked answer: Allegheny Ludlum alloy is the stainless-type material with high yield strength.
x.B: Nitralloy is a nitriding steel.
x.C: Nimonic is a nickel-base alloy for high-temperature service.
x.D: Inconel is a nickel-base alloy for high-temperature service.

questions.q: Which term refers to the vector change in position of an object with respect to a reference point?
questions.e: Displacement is a vector (straight-line change in position). Path length and speed are scalars; rate of change of velocity is acceleration.

x.A: Displacement is the vector change in position of an object relative to a reference point.
x.B: Path length is a scalar.
x.C: Speed is a scalar.
x.D: The rate of change of velocity is acceleration.

questions.q: Which component of acceleration is directed inward toward the center of rotation in circular motion?
questions.e: Radial (centripetal) acceleration = v²/r = ω²r, pointing toward the center.

x.A: Radial (centripetal) acceleration points inward toward the center of rotation.
x.B: Tangential acceleration acts along the path, not toward the center.
x.C: Translational acceleration describes straight-line motion.
x.D: Angular acceleration is the rate of change of angular velocity.

questions.q: The instantaneous center of rotation of a rigid thin disc rolling without slip on a plane rigid surface is located at
c: an infinite distance perpendicular to the plane surface
the point on the circumference situated vertically opposite to the contact point
questions.e: With no slip, the contact point has zero instantaneous velocity, so it is the instantaneous center.

x.A: The center of the disc moves, so it is not momentarily at rest.
x.B: An infinite distance would mean pure translation, not rolling.
x.C: With no slip the contact point has zero instantaneous velocity, so it is the instantaneous center.
x.D: The point opposite the contact moves at twice the center's speed.

questions.q: For a 4-bar linkage in toggle position, the value of mechanical advantage is
questions.e: At toggle, the output link is momentarily stationary for any input motion, so a tiny input force produces a very large output force: MA → ∞.

x.A: At the toggle position the output link is momentarily stationary, so the mechanical advantage tends to infinity.
x.B: A value of 0.5 is not what toggle gives.
x.C: A value of 1 is not what toggle gives.
x.D: Zero would mean no force is delivered, the opposite of toggle.

questions.q: It is a failure prediction theory which states that a part subjected to any combination of loads will fail (by yielding or fracturing) whenever the maximum shear stress exceeds a critical value. How do you call this failure prediction theory?
questions.e: Maximum-shear-stress (Tresca) theory: failure when τmax ≥ Sy/2.

x.A: Distortion-energy theory is von Mises, a different criterion.
x.B: The maximum-shear-stress (Tresca) theory predicts failure when the maximum shear stress reaches a critical value.
x.C: Internal friction theory is a theory for brittle materials.
x.D: Modified Mohr is a theory for brittle materials.

questions.q: Which standard governs the design and installation of piping systems typically used in process plants and industrial facilities?
questions.e: Marked answer: ASME B31.9 (Building Services Piping, covering industrial, commercial and institutional facilities). Note: process-plant piping proper is ASME B31.3, which is not among the choices. B31.1 is power piping; API 570 is in-service inspection; Section II is materials.

x.A: Marked answer: ASME B31.9 covers building services piping, including industrial and institutional facilities.
x.B: B31.1 is power piping.
x.C: API 570 is in-service piping inspection.
x.D: ASME Section II covers materials.

questions.q: The ratio of the fatigue strength of a polished specimen to the fatigue strength of a notched specimen at the same number of cycles is known as the
questions.e: Fatigue notch factor Kf = unnotched fatigue strength / notched fatigue strength. Notch sensitivity q = (Kf−1)/(Kt−1) is a different quantity.

x.A: Fatigue factor is not the standard name for this ratio.
x.B: The fatigue notch factor Kf is the unnotched fatigue strength divided by the notched strength.
x.C: Notch sensitivity q is a different quantity.
x.D: The stress concentration factor Kt is the theoretical factor from geometry.

questions.q: For large-scale production, which steel forming process is considered the most cost-efficient?
questions.e: Rolling is continuous and high-throughput, giving the lowest cost per ton for plate, bar and sections.

x.A: Rolling is continuous and high throughput, so it has the lowest cost per ton at large scale.
x.B: Cold forming gives a better finish but costs more.
x.C: Hot working includes rolling but is a general term.
x.D: Forging is slower and costlier, used for strong shaped parts.

questions.q: When one or more springs or resisting members share the load, the relative stiffness is known as
questions.e: Rigidity (stiffness) determines how the load divides among members: stiffer members take a larger share.

x.A: Rigidity (stiffness) decides how load is divided among members: stiffer members take more.
x.B: Elasticity is the ability to recover after loading.
x.C: Modulus is a material constant, not the load sharing.
x.D: Flexural rigidity (EI) is specific to beam bending.

questions.q: It is a correction factor used to account for nonuniform stress distributions.
questions.e: The stress concentration factor corrects the nominal stress for local peaks at holes, notches, fillets and other geometry changes.

x.A: The fatigue stress concentration factor is the fatigue-specific factor, not the general nonuniform-stress factor.
x.B: The geometric stress concentration factor is the theoretical Kt.
x.C: Marked answer: the stress concentration factor corrects for local stress peaks at holes, notches and fillets.
x.D: Stress correction factor is not the standard term.

questions.q: Fatigue failure occurs when a part is subjected to:
questions.e: Fatigue failure results from repeated or fluctuating (cyclic) stress, even well below the static strength.

x.A: A steady compressive stress does not cause fatigue.
x.B: A steady tensile stress does not cause fatigue.
x.C: A steady torsional stress does not cause fatigue.
x.D: Fluctuating (cyclic) stress causes fatigue failure, even well below static strength.

questions.q: A kinematic chain needs a minimum:
questions.e: The simplest constrained chain is the four-bar: 4 links joined by 4 turning pairs.

x.A: Two links and two pairs cannot form a closed chain.
x.B: Three links form a rigid triangle with no relative motion.
x.C: The four-bar, with 4 links and 4 turning pairs, is the simplest constrained chain.
x.D: Three links with two pairs form an open chain.

questions.q: On a pressure vessel nameplate, which designation indicates that the welds have been fully examined by radiographic testing?
questions.e: RT-1 = full radiography of the required welds. RT-2 to RT-4 mean partial, spot or no radiography. PWHT is post-weld heat treatment.

x.A: RT-1 means the required welds are fully radiographed.
x.B: RT-2 is partial radiography.
x.C: PWHT means post-weld heat treatment.
x.D: NDE is a general term for non-destructive examination.

questions.q: The total permissible variation in the size of a dimension: the difference between the limits of size.
questions.e: Tolerance = upper limit − lower limit. Allowance is the intended difference between mating parts.

x.A: Allowance is the intended difference between mating parts.
x.B: Tolerance is the total permissible variation: upper limit minus lower limit.
x.C: Variance is a statistical term.
x.D: Interference is a negative clearance.

questions.q: How many independent motions can a rigid body have when moved freely in space?
questions.e: Three translations plus three rotations = 6 degrees of freedom.

x.A: A free body has 6 degrees of freedom: three translations and three rotations.
x.B: 5 is too few for a free body.
x.C: 7 is too many.
x.D: 9 is too many.

questions.q: Which code is commonly used as a reference for the inspection, repair, and maintenance of pressure vessels in refinery and petrochemical service?
questions.e: API 510 is the Pressure Vessel Inspection Code (in-service inspection, repair, alteration, rerating). API 653 is for storage tanks; API 571 is damage mechanisms; Section VIII is construction.

x.A: API 510 is the pressure vessel inspection code for in-service inspection, repair and rerating.
x.B: API 653 is for storage tanks.
x.C: API 571 describes damage mechanisms.
x.D: ASME Section VIII covers construction, not in-service inspection.

questions.q: In general, the design stress and factor of safety are related as follows:
c: Design stress = ultimate stress times factor of safety
Design stress = ultimate stress divided by factor of safety
Design stress = design stress divided by ultimate stress
Design stress = factor of safety divided by design stress
questions.e: σd = σu / N.

x.A: Multiplying ultimate stress by the factor of safety would give a stress above ultimate.
x.B: Design stress = ultimate stress divided by the factor of safety.
x.C: Dividing design stress by ultimate stress does not define the relation.
x.D: This is not the relationship.

questions.q: The total deformation measured in the direction of the line of stress.
questions.e: Marked answer: strain, defined here as the total deformation in the direction of the stress. (Unit strain = deformation per unit length.)

x.A: Axial deformation is the change in length along the axis; it is a close idea but not the marked answer.
x.B: Elongation is the increase in length.
x.C: Marked answer: strain, the deformation in the direction of the stress.
x.D: Unit stress is stress per unit area.

questions.q: The maximum stress to which a material can be subjected without a trace of any permanent set remaining upon a complete withdrawal of the stress.
questions.e: Elastic limit: the largest stress from which the material fully recovers. Proportional limit is where stress stops being linear with strain.

x.A: The ultimate limit is the maximum stress before fracture.
x.B: The proportional limit is where stress stops being linear with strain.
x.C: The endurance limit relates to fatigue.
x.D: The elastic limit is the largest stress from which the material fully recovers.

questions.q: Which type of polyethylene exhibits the highest degree of crystallinity, resulting in greater stiffness, strength, and higher softening temperature?
questions.e: HDPE has little chain branching, so chains pack tightly into crystalline regions.

x.A: HDPE has little chain branching, so its chains pack tightly into crystalline regions.
x.B: Cross-linked PEX has chains tied together, which reduces crystallinity.
x.C: ULDPE is highly branched, so it has low crystallinity.
x.D: Amorphous polyethylene has no crystalline order.

questions.q: A soft material ______
c: Exhibits a high modulus of elasticity
Does not exhibit high modulus of elasticity
Does not yield greatly before breaking
questions.e: Marked answer: a soft material does not have a high modulus of elasticity (it deforms easily under load).

x.A: A high modulus describes a stiff material, not a soft one.
x.B: Yielding greatly before breaking describes a ductile material.
x.C: Marked answer: a soft material does not have a high modulus of elasticity.
x.D: Not yielding greatly describes a brittle material.

questions.q: Strain energy is a measure of
c: The ratio of ultimate failure strain to yielding strain
Energy per unit volume stored in a deformed material
Strain energy per unit volume to reach the yield point
questions.e: Strain energy is the energy stored in a body by deformation; per unit volume it is the area under the stress-strain curve.

x.A: The ratio of ultimate to yield strain is not strain energy.
x.B: Strain energy per unit volume is the energy stored in a deformed material, the area under the stress-strain curve.
x.C: Total plastic strain at failure is not strain energy.
x.D: Energy per unit volume up to yield is the modulus of resilience.

questions.q: For any specific material, the percentage decrease in diameter is known as
questions.e: Lateral (transverse) strain = change in diameter / original diameter. Poisson's ratio = lateral strain / longitudinal strain.

x.A: Axial strain is along the loading direction.
x.B: Diametral strain is the change in diameter over the original diameter; it is the same quantity as lateral strain.
x.C: Lateral strain is the change in diameter over the original diameter.
x.D: Longitudinal strain is along the length.

questions.q: The maximum stress induced in a material when subjected to alternate or repeated loading without causing failure.
questions.e: Endurance limit: the stress below which the material survives an effectively infinite number of cycles.

x.A: The yield point is where plastic deformation begins.
x.B: The ultimate point is the maximum stress.
x.C: The endurance limit is the stress the material can take under repeated loading without failure.
x.D: The proportional limit is where stress stops being linear with strain.

questions.q: The ability of metal to withstand forces thus following a number of twists.
questions.e: Marked answer: shear strength, because twisting (torsion) loads a material in shear.

x.A: Marked answer: shear strength, since twisting (torsion) loads a material in shear.
x.B: Bearing strength is about crushing under contact, not twisting.
x.C: The endurance limit relates to repeated loading, not twisting.
x.D: Deformation is a change in shape, not a strength property.

questions.q: A coating material used to produce galvanized iron
questions.e: Galvanizing is a zinc coating on iron or steel.

x.A: Zirconium is not used to galvanize iron.
x.B: Galvanizing is a zinc coating on iron or steel.
x.C: Aluminum coats steel in aluminizing, not galvanizing.
x.D: Chromium is used for chrome plating.

questions.q: Materials have a yield strength of 450 MPa and an ultimate strength of 700 MPa. If it is subjected to a tensile stress of 500 MPa, at what stage of the stress-strain curve is the material likely operating?
c: Plastic region before reaching ultimate strength
questions.e: 500 MPa exceeds the 450 MPa yield but is below the 700 MPa ultimate, so the material is in the plastic region before ultimate strength.

x.A: 500 MPa is above the 450 MPa yield and below the 700 MPa ultimate, so it is in the plastic region.
x.B: The elastic region is below the 450 MPa yield.
x.C: Fracture happens at the breaking stress.
x.D: Strain hardening beyond ultimate would be past 700 MPa.

questions.q: Which kinematic principle states that the instantaneous centers of three bodies in plane motion lie on a straight line?
questions.e: Kennedy's (Aronhold-Kennedy) theorem: the three instantaneous centers of three relatively moving bodies are collinear.

x.A: Kennedy's theorem says the three instant centers of three bodies in relative plane motion lie on a straight line.
x.B: Gruebler's equation gives degrees of freedom.
x.C: D'Alembert's principle relates to dynamic equilibrium.
x.D: Hooke's law relates stress and strain.

questions.q: According to code requirements, what is the minimum allowable thickness (inches), excluding corrosion allowance, for pressure vessels used in steam service?
questions.e: Marked answer: 1/16 in, the general minimum thickness in ASME Section VIII (UG-16). Note: UG-16 lists 3/32 in for vessels in compressed air, steam and water service, so confirm against your code edition or source.

x.A: Marked answer: 1/16 in is the general minimum thickness given for pressure vessels.
x.B: 1/8 in is not the marked value.
x.C: 3/32 in is the figure UG-16 lists for compressed air, steam and water service, so check your code edition.
x.D: 1/4 in is not the marked value.

questions.q: The property of steel which resists indention or penetration.
questions.e: Hardness is resistance to indentation or penetration.

x.A: Hardness is resistance to indentation or penetration.
x.B: Elasticity is the ability to return to shape after loading.
x.C: Ductility is the ability to stretch before breaking.
x.D: Hardness is the correct property.

questions.q: The hardness of steel increases if it contains:
questions.e: Martensite is the hardest microstructure in steel. Pearlite and austenite are softer.

x.A: Martensite is the hardest microstructure in steel.
x.B: Pearlite is softer.
x.C: Austenite is soft.
x.D: Not all of these raise hardness.

questions.q: Fatigue failure occurs when a part is subjected to:
questions.e: Fluctuating (cyclic) stress causes progressive crack growth and fatigue fracture.

x.A: Compressive stress alone does not cause fatigue.
x.B: Tensile stress alone does not cause fatigue.
x.C: Torsional stress alone does not cause fatigue.
x.D: Fluctuating stress causes progressive cracking and fatigue fracture.

questions.q: Which steel type is specifically designed for service at elevated temperatures, offering strong resistance to creep, oxidation, and corrosion?
questions.e: Marked answer: valve steel, a heat-resisting steel (e.g., for exhaust valves) with oxidation, corrosion and creep resistance at high temperature. Tool steel and maraging steel are not high-temperature service steels.

x.A: Marked answer: valve steel is a heat-resisting steel with oxidation, corrosion and creep resistance at high temperature.
x.B: Creep-resistant steel is also for high temperature, so some references prefer it here.
x.C: Tool steel is for cutting tools, not high-temperature service.
x.D: Maraging steel is an ultra-high-strength steel, not an elevated-temperature one.

questions.q: Which material does NOT exhibit a distinct endurance limit under cyclic loading?
questions.e: Marked answer: aluminum. Its S-N curve keeps sloping downward, so fatigue strength is quoted at a set number of cycles (e.g., 5×10⁸) rather than as a true endurance limit. Steels and irons show a distinct knee.

x.A: Marked answer: aluminum has no distinct endurance limit; its S-N curve keeps sloping down.
x.B: Titanium shows an endurance limit.
x.C: Copper also lacks a sharp endurance limit, so this question has two arguable answers.
x.D: Iron and steels show a distinct knee in the S-N curve.

questions.q: Which engine cycle best represents a diesel engine?
questions.e: Heat is added at constant pressure and rejected at constant volume: the Diesel cycle.

questions.q: Which component converts engine mechanical output to electricity?
questions.e: The alternator (generator) converts shaft mechanical power into electrical power.

questions.q: Which fuel injection system is widely used in modern diesel engines for precise control?
questions.e: Common-rail systems keep fuel at high pressure in a shared rail with electronically controlled injectors, giving precise timing, pressure and multiple injections.

questions.q: What parameter is primarily indicated by cetane number of diesel fuel?
questions.e: Cetane number measures how readily diesel fuel auto-ignites (ignition delay). Anti-knock quality is the octane number for gasoline.

questions.q: Which type of alternator is most common in gensets?
questions.e: Gensets use synchronous alternators because they give controllable voltage and frequency and can run in parallel.

questions.q: What parameter primarily affects Diesel cycle efficiency?
questions.e: Diesel efficiency depends on compression ratio and cut-off ratio; at a fixed compression ratio, a larger cut-off ratio lowers efficiency.

questions.q: What does octane number represent?
questions.e: Octane number rates a spark-ignition fuel's resistance to knock (detonation).

questions.q: What is the usual frequency of grid-synchronized diesel plants in many countries?
questions.e: Power grids operate at 50 Hz or 60 Hz (the Philippines uses 60 Hz).

questions.q: Which device protects the engine from overspeed during load rejection?
questions.e: The overspeed trip shuts down the engine (fuel cut-off) when speed exceeds a set limit. The AVR regulates voltage.

questions.q: What does the term "black start" refer to in diesel power plants?
questions.e: Black start means starting the plant from a dead (blackout) condition using its own batteries or air start, without outside power.

questions.q: Which emission is MAINLY reduced by Exhaust Gas Recirculation (EGR)?
questions.e: EGR dilutes the intake charge and lowers peak combustion temperature, which reduces thermal NOx formation.

questions.q: Which control ensures equal kW sharing among multiple generators?
questions.e: Governor droop makes speed fall slightly with load, so paralleled sets share real power (kW). AVR droop shares reactive power (kVAR).

questions.q: Which instrument measures insulation resistance of generator windings?
questions.e: A megger applies high DC voltage to measure insulation resistance.

questions.q: What is the likely cause of blue exhaust smoke?
questions.e: Blue smoke indicates lubricating oil burning in the cylinder (worn rings, valve guides, turbo seals). Black = rich or incomplete combustion; white = unburnt fuel or water.

questions.q: Which standard commonly covers on-site generator installation practices (electrical)?
questions.e: NFPA 110 covers emergency and standby power systems (generator installation, testing and maintenance).

questions.q: Which device measures generator reactive power?
questions.e: A VAR meter measures reactive power (kVAR).

questions.q: Which type of gas turbine cycle is also called the Brayton cycle?
questions.e: Brayton cycle = constant-pressure heat addition and rejection with isentropic compression and expansion.

questions.q: Which component compresses the inlet air in a gas turbine?
questions.e: The compressor raises the air pressure before combustion.

questions.q: Which cycle modification improves gas turbine efficiency by cooling compressed air before combustion?
questions.e: Intercooling between compressor stages cuts compressor work (and lowers temperature). Strictly it raises net work; the question's intended answer is intercooling.

questions.q: What is the function of an intercooler in a multistage compressor?
questions.e: Cooling the air between stages reduces its specific volume, so later stages need less work.

questions.q: What is the effect of reheating in a gas turbine cycle?
questions.e: Reheating between turbine stages increases turbine work and thus net specific work output (while fuel use rises).

questions.q: Which cycle efficiency increases by regeneration?
questions.e: Regeneration recovers exhaust heat to preheat compressed air, lowering fuel needed and raising thermal efficiency.

questions.q: Which type of compressor is generally used in aircraft gas turbines?
questions.e: Axial-flow compressors give high mass flow and high pressure ratio with small frontal area.

questions.q: Which combustion chamber type is commonly used in stationary gas turbines?
questions.e: Heavy-duty stationary turbines commonly use can-annular (cannular) combustors: individual cans arranged around the shaft inside an annular casing. (Older industrial units used separate can/tubular types.)

questions.q: Which law relates stagnation temperature rise in compressors to work input?
questions.e: From the steady-flow energy equation, W = c p (T 02 - T 01 ) for an adiabatic compressor.

questions.q: What is the effect of regeneration on turbine exhaust temperature?
questions.e: Exhaust heat is transferred to the compressed air, so the gas leaving the regenerator (stack temperature) is lower.

questions.q: Which cycle is used in jet propulsion gas turbines?
questions.e: Jet engines take in and discharge atmospheric air, so they follow the open Brayton cycle.

questions.q: Which cycle efficiency is highest theoretically among Brayton, Otto, and Diesel for same compression ratio?
questions.e: At the same compression ratio, Otto (constant volume heat addition) has the highest efficiency; Diesel is lower because of its cut-off ratio. (The source choices were mislabeled A, D, C, D; arranged here as A to D.)

questions.q: What is the effect of pressure ratio increasing beyond optimum in gas turbines?
questions.e: Beyond the optimum, compressor work grows faster than turbine work (and component losses grow), so net output and actual efficiency fall.

questions.q: Which part of gas turbine requires most maintenance?
questions.e: Turbine blades face high temperature, centrifugal stress, creep, corrosion and erosion, so they need the most inspection and replacement. (The combustor is also a hot-section part.)

questions.q: What is the usual firing order in multiple combustor gas turbines?
questions.e: Ignition starts in one or two combustors and the flame spreads to the others in sequence through cross-fire tubes.

questions.q: What is the primary pollutant formed at high turbine inlet temperatures?
questions.e: Thermal NOx forms rapidly at high flame temperature.

questions.q: What primarily affects the thermal efficiency of a gas turbine plant?
questions.e: Ideal Brayton efficiency = 1 - 1/r p (k-1)/k .

questions.q: What is the working principle of a steam power plant?
questions.e: Steam power plants operate on the Rankine cycle.

questions.q: Which component of a steam power plant generates steam by burning fuel?
questions.e: The boiler (steam generator) burns fuel to convert feedwater into steam.

questions.q: Which device increases the temperature of steam above saturation temperature?
questions.e: The superheater adds heat to dry saturated steam, raising it above saturation temperature.

questions.q: Which type of boiler is commonly used in large steam power plants?
questions.e: Water-tube boilers handle high pressures and large capacities.

questions.q: What is the function of an economizer?
c: To preheat feedwater using flue gas
questions.e: The economizer recovers flue-gas heat to preheat boiler feedwater.

questions.q: Which type of condenser is used in most large plants?
questions.e: Surface (shell-and-tube) condensers keep the condensate separate from cooling water, so it can be reused as feedwater.

questions.q: Which device is used to remove scales and sludge from boiler?
questions.e: The blowdown valve drains sludge and concentrated dissolved solids from the boiler.

questions.q: Which cycle modification improves efficiency by extracting steam?
questions.e: In a regenerative cycle, steam bled from the turbine heats the feedwater.

questions.q: Which device ensures boiler water does not overheat the furnace?
questions.e: The fusible plug melts when the water level is dangerously low, releasing steam to warn of and prevent overheating.

questions.q: What should be done to decrease heat rejected in a steam plant?
questions.e: Lowering condenser temperature (pressure) increases turbine work for the same heat input, so heat rejected per unit of work is lower.

questions.q: Which auxiliary increases boiler efficiency by heating combustion air?
questions.e: The air preheater recovers flue-gas heat to warm the combustion air.

questions.q: Which method reduces scaling in boiler tubes?
questions.e: Water treatment removes scale-forming hardness, and blowdown removes concentrated solids.

questions.q: Which component regulates steam flow to turbine?
questions.e: The governor (throttle) valve controls steam admission to match load and speed.

questions.q: Which loss is highest in coal-fired boilers?
questions.e: Heat carried away by dry flue gas is typically the largest boiler loss.

questions.q: Which method improves boiler combustion efficiency?
questions.e: Optimum excess air ensures complete combustion without excess flue-gas loss.

questions.q: Which type of condenser has better water economy?
questions.e: In a surface condenser the condensate is recovered and returned to the boiler. (A dry/air-cooled condenser uses no cooling water but is a special-purpose type.)

questions.q: Which section of Rankine cycle improves by regeneration?
questions.e: Regeneration improves the feedwater heating section by using extracted steam to raise feedwater temperature.

questions.q: In bolts design, the quotient of the proof load and the tensile-stress area is called
questions.e: Proof strength = proof load / tensile-stress area.

questions.q: In clutch analysis, which assumption is generally used for torque calculations?
questions.e: For design, the uniform wear assumption is used because it is more conservative and applies once the plates have worn in.

questions.q: It is the distance in inches a screw thread (a helix) advances axially in one turn.
questions.e: Lead is the axial advance per turn. (It equals the pitch only for a single-start thread.)

questions.q: What type of bolt distinguished by a short portion of the shank underneath the head being square or finned or ribbed?
questions.e: A carriage bolt has a square, finned or ribbed neck under its rounded head that keeps it from turning when the nut is tightened.

questions.q: If the friction angle in a screw exceeds the lead angle, what behavior is exhibited?
questions.e: When φ > λ (tanφ = µ), the load cannot back-drive the screw, so it is self-locking.

questions.q: Which thread form is most suitable for power transmission in lifting devices like screw jacks?
questions.e: Square threads have the highest efficiency and no radial (bursting) load on the nut, which suits lifting screws (marked answer on the paper).

questions.q: Which type of clutch transmits torque through direct engagement of interlocking elements?
questions.e: Positive clutches (jaw, claw, toothed) transmit torque by mechanical interlock instead of friction.

questions.q: Under uniform wear theory, how does pressure vary along the radius of a clutch plate?
c: It becomes zero at the center
questions.e: Uniform wear gives p·r = constant, so pressure is highest at the inner radius and decreases outward.

questions.q: A coupling that allows axial flexibility/movement in the operation. Made of alternate bolting of steel, leather, fabric and/or plastic material into two flanges.
questions.e: Marked answer on the paper is C. Note that the description (alternating bolted layers of steel, leather, fabric or plastic between two flanges) sounds like a flexible disk coupling in some references, so confirm with your reviewer.

questions.q: The crest diameter of a screw thread is the same as:
questions.e: The crests of an external thread are at its largest diameter, the major (outside) diameter.

questions.q: For an American Standard Screw Threads, what does 6-32 UNC designate?
c: Size 6, 32 threads per inch, coarse thread
6 inches basic diameter, 32 threads per inch, coarse thread
Size 6, 32 threads per inch, fine thread
32 inches basic diameter, 6 threads per inch, coarse thread
questions.e: 6 is the screw size number, 32 is threads per inch, and UNC means Unified National Coarse.

questions.q: In braking, the term backstop refers to a brake that is:
questions.e: A backstop (non-reversing device) lets the shaft turn freely one way and locks it against rotating the other way.

questions.q: A tool bit for cutting an American National thread should be ground with an angle of:
questions.e: American National (and Unified) threads have a 60° included thread angle.

questions.q: What type of compound screw which produces a motion equal to the difference in motion between the two component screws?
questions.e: A differential screw has two threads of slightly different lead, so the net advance per turn is the difference between them.

questions.q: A screw that requires positive torque to lower the load, or to loosen the screw if it has been turned tight against a resistance.
questions.e: This describes a self-locking screw: the load cannot turn it back, so torque must be applied to lower or loosen it.

questions.q: In the application of this fastener, a pin is inserted into a hole and a metal collar is place over the end.
questions.e: A Huckbolt is a lockbolt: a grooved pin goes through the hole and a collar is swaged over the end.

questions.q: Which of the following type of fastener has a trilobe thread structure?
questions.e: Taptite screws have a trilobular (three-lobed) cross-section that forms threads by cold rolling.

questions.q: In general, to engage securely and prevent dragging, what is the clearance between release bearing and release collar in the clutch?
questions.e: Marked answer: about 2–3 mm of free clearance so the bearing does not drag when the clutch is engaged.

questions.q: The function of clutch in the machine tools is:
c: To disconnect or connect at will the drive
To ensure that two shafts line up at high speed
questions.e: A clutch lets the operator couple or uncouple the driven shaft from the drive at will.

questions.q: Type of setscrew that is used where frequent adjustment is necessary between the two parts that are secured.
questions.e: Flat-pointed setscrews cause the least damage to the shaft, so the parts can be readjusted often.

questions.q: Type of setscrew usually used where the two joined parts are to have permanent position with respect to each other.
questions.e: The cone point digs into a spot on the shaft, giving a strong, permanent hold.

questions.q: Most widely used type of setscrew.
questions.e: The cup point is the most common general-purpose setscrew.

questions.q: The differential screw is used in a
questions.e: Differential screws give very fine motion, as in micrometer-type adjusters (marked answer on the paper).

questions.q: Which of the following is an effective method of reducing the alternating stress in bolted tension connections?
questions.e: Preloading keeps the joint clamped so that the bolt sees only a small part of the fluctuating load, which lowers the alternating stress.

questions.q: For bolts, the proof load is slightly less than the
questions.e: Proof load is the maximum load a bolt can carry without permanent deformation, so it is just below the yield strength.

questions.q: The torque coefficient for lubricated bolts generally varies from
questions.e: Marked answer on the paper. The torque coefficient K in T = KDF is about 0.2 for typical bolts, and a bit lower with lubrication.

questions.q: The maximum efficiency of self-locking screw is
questions.e: For a self-locking screw (φ ≥ λ), efficiency can be at most 50%.

questions.q: Which of the following screw thread is adopted for power transmission in either direction?
questions.e: ACME threads are used for power transmission in both directions (marked answer on the paper). Buttress threads carry load in one direction only.

questions.q: In case of power screws, what is the combination of materials used for the screw and the nut?
c: Cast iron screw and mild steel nut
Carbon steel screw and phosphor bronze nut
Cast iron screw and cast-iron nut
Aluminum screw and alloy steel nut
questions.e: A steel screw with a bronze nut gives a low-friction, wear-resistant pair, and the cheaper nut wears out instead of the screw.

questions.q: For most bolt sizes with a coefficient of friction of 0.15, the torque coefficient is approximately
questions.e: Marked answer: K ≈ 0.20 for typical bolts in T = KDF.

questions.q: Brake that requires some finite application force
questions.e: Marked answer on the paper. A self-energizing brake uses friction to help apply itself but still needs some initial application force.

questions.q: On the motors with low starting toque, the type of the clutch to be used is
questions.e: A centrifugal clutch only engages once the motor has speeded up, so the motor starts with almost no load.

questions.q: These clutches produce positive coupling between the two shafts, regardless of direction of rotation.
questions.e: Jaw clutches engage by mechanical interlock, giving positive drive with no slip.

questions.q: If the clutch assembly is known to be semiflexible, what distribution can be assumed?
questions.e: Marked answer on the paper. Uniform pressure applies to new or flexible assemblies, while uniform wear applies to rigid, worn-in ones.

questions.q: Which of the following brake does not require external application force?
questions.e: A self-locking brake holds itself on through friction and needs no external force to stay applied.

questions.q: In a block brake, the pressure will be distributed approximately uniformly if the block contact angle is less than
questions.e: Pressure is roughly uniform for block contact angles under 60°.

questions.q: Which of the following is a device use to connect an initially stationary shaft to a rotating shaft?
questions.e: A clutch can engage a stationary shaft with a rotating one while the drive keeps running.

questions.q: Which of the following clutches that has a disadvantage of heavier rotating masses?
questions.e: A multiple disc clutch has many plates, which adds rotating mass and inertia.

questions.q: Which one of the following is not a friction clutch?
questions.e: The jaw clutch is a positive (interlocking) clutch, not a friction clutch.

questions.q: The effect of increasing the stiffness of springs of centrifugal clutch is
c: The increase of frictional force at maximum speed
questions.e: Stiffer springs hold the shoes in longer, so the shaft must spin faster before the clutch engages.

questions.q: What type of bolt threaded on both ends and can be used where a through bolt impossible?
questions.e: A stud bolt is threaded on both ends and screws into a tapped hole where a through bolt can't be used.

questions.q: To avoid self-engagement in cone clutch, its semi-cone angle is always kept
c: smaller than the angle of static friction
equal to the angle of static friction
greater than the angle of static friction
half of the angle of static friction
questions.e: Marked answer on the paper. A cone angle larger than the friction angle lets the clutch release easily and not lock itself in.

questions.q: Clutch slippage while clutch is engaged is especially noticeable.
questions.e: Slip shows most under high torque demand, which is during acceleration.

questions.q: In bolts design, proof strength corresponds approximately how many percent of the 0.2 percent offset yield strength?
questions.e: Marked answer on the paper: proof strength is about 90% of the 0.2% offset yield strength.

questions.q: A brake commonly used in railway trains is
questions.e: Railway trains use shoe (block) brakes pressing on the wheel tread.

questions.q: A type of key in which width and thickness are equal is called as:
questions.e: A square key has a square cross-section, so its width equals its thickness (w = t). A flat key is wider than it is thick.

questions.q: While designing a parallel sunk key it is assumed that the distribution of force along the length of the key:
c: varies exponentially, being more at the torque input end
varies exponentially, being less at the torque output end
questions.e: Standard key design assumes the load (shear and crushing) is spread uniformly along the key length.

questions.q: What type of key allows the hub to move along the shaft but prevents the rotation of the shaft?
questions.e: A feather key is fixed to the shaft (or hub) and the mating part slides along it, so axial motion is allowed while torque is still transmitted.

questions.q: The speed at which the center of mass will be equal the deflecting forces on the shaft; the shaft with its attached bodies will then vibrate violently since the centrifugal force changes its direction as the shaft turns in:
questions.e: At the critical (whirling) speed the shaft's natural frequency matches the rotational speed, causing resonance and violent vibration.

questions.q: Which device is primarily used to prevent axial movement of components like gears or pulleys along a shaft?
questions.e: A retaining ring (circlip) seats in a groove on the shaft and locks parts axially. Keys transmit torque; they do not hold parts axially.

questions.q: Which type of key is used for mounting shifting gears in gear boxes?
questions.e: Splines transmit torque while letting the gear slide axially along the shaft to shift.

questions.q: It is used for permanent fits and similar to involute splines except that the pressure angle is 14.5 deg.
questions.e: Involute serrations resemble involute splines but with a 45° flank / 14.5° pressure angle and are used for permanent press fits.

questions.q: What is the maximum shaft angle for a single Hooke's coupling?
questions.e: As the angle between shafts increases, speed fluctuation grows. A single Hooke's joint is generally limited to about 15° (marked answer on the paper).

questions.q: Universal coupling is:
questions.e: A universal joint connects shafts whose axes intersect at an angle (non-collinear).

questions.q: What is the primary function of a shaft coupling in mechanical systems?
c: To prevent relative motion between shafts
To transmit power between two shafts
To absorb all vibration in the system
questions.e: A coupling joins two shafts so power/torque passes from the driving shaft to the driven shaft.

questions.q: Splines are used when:
c: The power to be transmitted is high
Axial relative motion between shafts and hub is necessary
questions.e: Splines carry torque while permitting axial sliding between shaft and hub.

questions.q: Allowance is defined as:
c: Difference between maximum hole and minimum shaft
Difference between minimum hole and maximum shaft
questions.e: Allowance is the intentional minimum clearance: smallest hole − largest shaft.

questions.q: A fit where clearance or interference may occur is called:
questions.e: In a transition fit the tolerance zones overlap, so the assembly may end up with either a small clearance or a small interference.

questions.q: Which type of coupling is commonly used for shafts that are properly aligned but need to be separated occasionally?
questions.e: Rigid couplings (e.g. flange or split-muff types) suit well-aligned shafts and can be unbolted when separation is needed.

questions.q: Maximum clearance is:
questions.e: Maximum clearance = largest hole − smallest shaft. (Smallest hole − largest shaft is the minimum clearance.)

questions.q: A negative clearance indicates:
questions.e: Negative clearance means the shaft is larger than the hole, which is an interference.

questions.q: In hole-basis system, which dimension is fixed?
questions.e: In the hole-basis system the hole's lower limit equals the basic size (fundamental deviation = 0, the 'H' hole).

questions.q: In shaft-basis system, which dimension is fixed?
questions.e: In the shaft-basis system the shaft's upper limit equals the basic size (the 'h' shaft).

questions.q: What does H7 indicate in ISO system?
questions.e: Capital letters denote holes. H is the position (fundamental deviation zero) and 7 is the IT tolerance grade.

questions.q: Which type of spline is generally recommended when slight misalignment between shaft and hub must be accommodated?
questions.e: Involute splines self-center and distribute load well, so they tolerate slight misalignment better.

questions.q: In fits and tolerance, what does “g6” represent?
questions.e: Lowercase letters denote shafts: g is the position (a small negative fundamental deviation) and 6 is the tolerance grade.

questions.q: Upper deviation is:
c: Difference between max size and basic size
Difference between min size and basic size
questions.e: Upper deviation = maximum limit of size − basic size. (Lower deviation uses the minimum limit.)

questions.q: What characterizes a flexible coupling?
c: It increases shaft rigidity during operation
It is used only for high-speed applications
It accommodates slight misalignment between shafts
questions.e: Flexible couplings tolerate small angular, parallel and axial misalignment and absorb some shock/vibration. They do not eliminate misalignment.

questions.q: In the design of machine keys used for torque transmission, which mode of failure is typically considered critical?
questions.e: Keys are designed mainly against shearing across the shaft-hub interface (and checked for crushing/bearing).

questions.q: Which torque-transmitting method depends on friction developed due to an interference between mating surfaces?
questions.e: A press fit grips by interference-generated contact pressure, so torque is carried by friction.

questions.q: Which type of key is most suitable when a hub must be accurately positioned against a shaft shoulder?
questions.e: The Woodruff key sits in a deep semicircular seat, so it stays put and is self-aligning (marked answer on the paper).

questions.q: Which fit is used for permanent assembly?
questions.e: A force (heavy press) fit has large interference and is for permanent assemblies that are not meant to be taken apart.

questions.q: Which system is most commonly used in manufacturing?
questions.e: Holes are made with standard tools (drills, reamers), so fixing the hole size and varying the shaft is cheaper and more practical.

questions.q: A fit with zero clearance and zero interference is called:
questions.e: A line fit means the mating surfaces just touch along a line, with no clearance and no interference.

questions.q: A rotating shaft subjected to combined bending and torsion should be designed using which failure theory?
questions.e: The classic shaft design equation (ASME code) uses the maximum shear stress theory, which is simple and conservative for ductile shafts (marked answer on the paper). Von Mises is also valid but less conservative.

questions.q: In applying the Goodman relation, which material is generally excluded due to its brittle nature when considering yield strength?
questions.e: Cast iron is brittle and has no well-defined yield point, so yield-based criteria don't apply to it.

questions.q: Which failure theory states that yielding begins when the octahedral shear stress reaches the value corresponding to yielding in simple tension?
questions.e: This is the distortion (shear) energy theory (von Mises–Hencky): yielding starts when the octahedral shear stress equals its value at yield in simple tension.

questions.q: In fatigue analysis, which factor depends purely on the shape or geometry of a component?
questions.e: The theoretical stress concentration factor Kt depends only on geometry. The fatigue strength reduction factor Kf also involves the material through notch sensitivity.

questions.q: What is the standard taper commonly used for a gib-head key in machine design?
questions.e: Marked answer on the paper is 1:48. Note that many textbooks give 1:100 for standard tapered keys, so go with what your reviewer/professor uses.

questions.q: Which failure theory considers the total strain energy stored in a material, including contributions from shear?
questions.e: The maximum strain energy (Haigh) theory uses total strain energy per unit volume, including both volume-change and shape-change parts.

questions.q: A stress varies between zero and a positive maximum value during a loading cycle. What type of stress condition is this?
questions.e: A cycle from zero to a maximum in one direction (minimum = 0) is repeated stress, a special case of fluctuating stress with R = 0.

questions.q: If both the maximum and minimum stresses are tensile but differ in magnitude, what type of stress cycle is present?
questions.e: Fluctuating stress has a non-zero mean with unequal max and min. Here both are tensile, so the mean is positive.

questions.q: Which design approach is most effective in minimizing stress concentration in mechanical components?
questions.e: Gradual transitions and generous fillet radii let the stress flow smoothly. Sharp corners, notches and abrupt changes raise stress concentration.

questions.q: Which statement best describes a rigid coupling?
c: It permits angular and parallel misalignment
It is used only for temporary shaft connections
It connects shafts without allowing any misalignment
It reduces torque transmitted between shafts
questions.e: A rigid coupling joins shafts into one solid unit, so it needs accurate alignment and cannot accommodate misalignment.

questions.q: Which type of key is most suitable when frequent removal of the hub is required without damaging the shaft?
questions.e: Marked answer on the paper is Woodruff key (easy to seat and remove, with a shallow keyway in the hub). A feather key is also commonly cited for sliding/removable hubs.

questions.q: Which type of pump is commonly used for viscous fluids like oil?
Which parameter represents the energy required at pump suction to avoid cavitation?
Which type of pump is classified as a positive displacement pump?
Which is the point where pump curve and system curve intersect?
